assembly_info.comments:
Background: The Leishmania aethiopica strain L147 (WHO strain identifier MHOM/ET/1972/L100) was obtained from Charles Jaffe (Israel). This parasite was isolated in Ethiopia in Wollega Province near to a place called Nekempti. It was obtained from a relapsing skin lesion of a 9-year old male, who was a classical case of diffuse cutaneous leishmaniasis (DCL); his skin test was negative (as is typical for DCL). The excreted factor (EF) sub-serotype is B1. Other designations for Strain LRC-L147 are LV24 (Liverpool School of Trop. Med. collection number). (Strain information provided by Lee Schnur, Israel). PCR tests using primers recognizing both LRV1 and LRV2 were negative. Genomic DNA was prepared by CsCl/Ethidium bromide density gradient centrifugation to minimize the amount of kinetoplast (mitochondrial) DNA, and was provided by Drs. Natalia Akopyants and Stephen Beverley, Washington University School of Medicine. The input sequence coverage of Illumina instrument fragment reads was 110X, while the final assembled coverage was 220X (fragments, 3 and 8kb) using a genome size estimate of 35Mb. The combined sequence reads were assembled using the ALLPATHS software (Broad Institute). This draft assembly is referred to as Leishmania aethiopica L147 2.0.3. This version has been cleaned of contaminating contigs, and the scaffolds were arranged into chromosomes. The assembly is made up of a total of 36 scaffolds with an N50 scaffold length of over 1.0Mb (N50 contig length was 38.3kb). The assembly spans 31Mb.
This work was supported by NIH grant AI29646 to SMB and by NIH-NHGRI grant 5U54HG00307907 to RKW, Director of The Genome Institute at Washington University.
For questions regarding this Leishmania aethiopica L147 2.0.3 assembly please contact Dr. Wesley Warren, Washington University School of Medicine (wwarren@genome.wustl.edu). Downloads of the sequence data are available via the TriTrypDB genome browser server. Funding for the sequence characterization of the Leishmania aethiopica L147 genome was provided by the National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI), National Institutes of Health (NIH).
Source DNA can be obtained by mailing: Stephen M. Beverley, Ph.D. Marvin A. Brennecke Professor and Head of Molecular Microbiology Department of Molecular Microbiology Campus Box 8230 Washington University School of Medicine 660 S. Euclid Ave. St. Louis, MO 63110 USA
